chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the captive whom the enemy takes from the Muslims during fighting, from the children of the Muslims or from their owned slaves, so they hold them. Then the Muslims afterwards fight them and gain victory over them, capture them, and take from them what they had taken from the owned slaves of the Muslims and their children whom they had taken from the Muslims. How should they be dealt with, from the children of the Muslims and their owned slaves?

He said, so he said: 'As for the children of the Muslims, they are not evaluated in the share of the Muslims, but they are returned to their father, or their brother, or to their guardian with witnesses. And as for the owned slaves, they are evaluated in the share of the Muslims, so they are sold and their masters are given the value of their price from the Public Treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.سِهَام: Shares (of the booty/captives distributed among fighters)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for Muslim children and slaves captured by enemies and later recaptured?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the distinct jurisprudential treatment of free Muslim children versus enslaved individuals in early Islamic military contexts, emphasizing the preservation of lineage and family integrity for the former. It reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of property rights and compensation mechanisms within the Bayt al-Mal, ensuring that the economic loss of enslaved owners is offset while keeping freeborn Muslims out of the general distribution of war spoils.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim,
(It has been narrated) from one of the companions of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

with regards to the captives taken from the Muslims during the fighting, from the children of the Muslims, or from their owned slaves, so they (enemies) hold them. Then Muslims, afterwards fight with them and capture them, and take from them, what they had taken, from the owned slaves of the Muslims and their children whom they (enemies) had taken from the Muslim, how should they be dealt with, from the children of the Muslims and their owned slaves.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the children of the Muslim, so they would not be evaluated in the share of the Muslims, but they would be returned to their fathers, or their brothers, or to their guardians with a witness. And as for the owned slaves, so they would be evaluated in the share of the Muslims, so they would be sold and their masters would be given their price from the Public Treasury of the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the Muslim prisoners, their children or servants (slaves), taken by the enemy who were afterwards rescued after a victorious fight, how should they be dealt with, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The children of the Muslims do not become the share of the Muslims. They are returned to their parents, or brothers, or their guardian in the presence of witnesses.
The slaves however become of the share of the Muslims. They are purchased with money from public treasury and their price is given to their owners.’”
